Descriptive comparison of matched native functional mixed-model residual diagnostics

etr_native_mixed_residual_comparison.Rd

Compare observed time-lag residual dependence of two explicitly matched, converged native functional mixed-moments or R/nlme joint B-spline likelihood models, preserving the frozen Python 1.2 source's diagnostic column keys and difference definitions.

Usage

etr_compare_functional_mixed_effects_residual_diagnostics(
  reference, comparison, max_lag,
  reference_label = "reference", comparison_label = "comparison",
  residual_scale = "raw"
)

Arguments

reference

Restricted native converged functional mixed-moments fit or native joint B-spline Gaussian likelihood fit.

comparison

Matched native converged mixed-moments or joint Gaussian likelihood fit with identical time grid, source curves, participants, observed time unit and response channel.

max_lag

Positive maximum index lag, smaller than grid length.

reference_label

Nonempty reference model label.

comparison_label

Nonempty comparison model label.

residual_scale

One of "raw" or "whitened".

Value

A descriptive data frame containing 0-based index lags and retained physical lag times, pair counts, source metrics from each model, and the comparison-minus-reference autocovariance, autocorrelation and semivariance.

Details

This supports either restricted native two-level functional moments or native R/nlme joint B-spline Gaussian fits without refitting them. The R joint estimator is not the full Python statsmodels mixed-effects maximum-likelihood/restricted-likelihood implementation. Input-domain, source result-type and underlying estimator differences are open. No automatic covariance model choice, hypothesis test, inferential calibration, one-to-one certification or source-equivalent MixedLM fit is claimed. Unmatched source curves, participants, time grids and lag support are rejected rather than silently dropped.
